correctness.rationale: Torus coincidence number equals |det(A^n-J^n)| when nonzero and infinity when the determinant vanishes. Cayley–Hamilton A^n=U_n A-U_(n-1)I gives off-diagonal difference δU_n, U_n=(λ^n−λ^-n)/sqrt(t²-4). For odd n=2k+1 det=2+(-1)^k δ U_n; even n=2k det=2−(-1)^k tr(A^n). With t>2, U3>=8 and tr(A^n)>2, only singular equality is n=1 and δ=-2. For δ=-1 at n=1 the ordinary sign formula needs the stated +2 correction; all other signs follow from size of U_n. Summing even and odd count power series yields the two explicit zeta germs. If δ=0, Z=(1+z)(1+z²)/((1-z)sqrt(D_t(z))) is algebraic nonrational, odd counts exactly 2 and even counts exponential, so liminf root 1 and limsup λ. If δ!=0,-2, the rational log-derivative has at z=i residue 1−i sgnδ, not rational; an algebraic germ Puiseux leading exponent would give rational residue. Thus Z is transcendental and both parities have exponential growth rate λ. Independent exact integer det(A^n−J^n) for sample trace t=3,4,5,6 and deltas 0,1,-1,-2,-3 for n=1..16 matched all boundaries; the analytic Puiseux argument proves the infinite assertion.
